You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Clearing the combobox never calls onChange(null), so the selection can't be cleared.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog: Escape inside a nested Dialog calls `onOpenChange(false)` on both dialogs. React portal events bubble through the outer `DialogContent.onKeyDown`, and the inner dialog does not stop propagation. Repro: outer `onOpenChange` spy called once with `false` after one Escape in the inner dialog. Failing line: `expect(outer).not.toHaveBeenCalled();` → "expected "spy" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times". Fix: `event.stopPropagation()` in the Escape branch of `Dialog.tsx`.
- [blocking] Dialog: `<input type="hidden">` is matched by the TABBABLE selector. Initial focus lands on the trigger, outside the dialog. Repro: `<Dialog open><form><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="x"/><button>one</button><button>two</button></form></Dialog>`. After opening, `document.activeElement` is the trigger `BUTTON[open] inDialog=false` (D3 fails). With the hidden input last, Tab from "two" leaves the dialog to `BODY` (D4 fails). Fix: exclude `input[type=hidden]` (and non-rendered elements) from `getTabbables`.
- [blocking, checklist: every aria-controls resolves] Tabs: every tab sets `aria-controls` to its panel id, but `TabPanel` returns null for unselected values. Repro: two tabs, `defaultValue="a"`; for tab "b", `aria-controls="«r0»-panel-b"` and `document.getElementById(...)` is null. Note this conflicts with T2 and T3 only if read strictly; the checklist requires the reference to exist. Options for the orchestrator: render unselected panels with `hidden`, or omit `aria-controls` on unselected tabs.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog D3/D5: opening dialog B while dialog A is open does not focus B (initial-focus guard skips it because the active element is in unrelated dialog A). Escape then closes A, not B. Repro: `fireEvent.click(OpenA); fireEvent.click(OpenB); fireEvent.keyDown(document.activeElement, {key:"Escape"})` gives `focus after B opened: ABtn`, `A closed: 1  B closed: 0`. Same failure when both are rendered open as React siblings (`expected 'ABtn' to be 'BBtn'`).
- [blocking] Dialog D4 nesting: an outer dialog with zero tabbables that contains an open inner dialog. Tab from the inner's last button moves focus to the outer dialog element. Repro: `screen.getByText("I2").focus(); user.keyboard("{Tab}")` gives `after Tab from I2 focus: dialog Outerno buttons`. The outer's Tab handler runs on the React-bubbled keydown and steals focus. Edge case, but the inner trap is broken.
- [minor] Dialog D5 backdrop: mousedown on backdrop, mouseup inside the dialog, then click (browsers fire it on the backdrop) closes the dialog (`onOpenChange` called once). The spec only forbids the reverse direction, so this is a UX nit, not a spec violation.
- [minor] FEATURE_FLOW.md is an untracked file in the repo root that the diff does not mention. Confirm it belongs in the change.
- [minor] Tabs controlled mode: arrow keys move DOM focus to a tab whose tabIndex is -1, because the tab stop stays on the controlled value. Not reproduced as a failure; expected by spec wording.
- [minor] Combobox README says Escape while closed "does nothing", but inside a Dialog it still closes the dialog (the event bubbles). The code is consistent; the wording could say so.

FIXES (decided — implement exactly):
1. Dialog nested Escape: in the Escape branch of `DialogContent`'s keydown handler, call `event.stopPropagation()` (and `preventDefault()`) so only the innermost dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` fires. 2. Dialog tabbables: exclude `input[type="hidden"]` from `getTabbables` (e.g. selector `input:not([type="hidden"])`). Test: `<form><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="x"/><button>one</button><button>two</button></form>` → initial focus on "one"; also with the hidden input last, Tab from "two" wraps to "one". Update README's tabbable list.
3. Tabs aria-controls must resolve: render every TabPanel, with the `hidden` attribute on unselected ones (instead of returning null). Panel still has role=tabpanel, id, aria-labelledby, tabIndex 0. Test: every tab's aria-controls resolves via document.getElementById; unselected panels are present but `hidden` (use `toBeVisible()`/`not.toBeVisible()` or check the attribute). 4. Dialog backdrop styling hook: add optional `backdropClassName?: string` prop applied to the backdrop div, and give the backdrop `data-dialog-backdrop=""` attribute. Export stays via DialogProps. README props table row. Test it.
5. Combobox clear to null: if the user has edited the text to empty (query === "" — trimmed empty is fine too) and then presses Enter or the input blurs, call `onChange(null)` (only if `value !== null`), then close. Enter with an empty query and an active option: the empty-query clear takes precedence ONLY when no option is active; if the user arrowed to an active option, Enter selects it as before. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Tabs
- T1 `Tabs` props: `defaultValue?: string`, `value?: string`, `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`, `children`. If `value` is provided it is controlled (internal state ignored; clicking/keys call `onValueChange` but selection only changes when parent updates `value`). Otherwise uncontrolled starting at `defaultValue`; if `defaultValue` is omitted, the first non-disabled tab is selected.
- T2 `TabList` renders `role="tablist"` with the passed `aria-label` (plus `aria-orientation="horizontal"` optional). `Tab value disabled?` renders a `<button type="button" role="tab">` with `aria-selected` true/false, `aria-controls` = its panel's id, `id` that the panel's `aria-labelledby` references. Disabled tab: `aria-disabled="true"` (or `disabled`), cannot be selected by click or keyboard.
- T3 `TabPanel value` renders `role="tabpanel"`, `aria-labelledby` = matching tab id, `tabIndex={0}`; only the selected panel is shown (non-selected panels are either not rendered or have `hidden`). Ids for tab/panel are derived from one `useId()` per Tabs instance plus the value, so tab and panel link up regardless of render order and two Tabs instances don't collide. Values containing spaces or special characters must still produce valid, matching ids (sanitize or index-map).
- T4 Roving tabindex: only the selected tab has `tabIndex=0`; all others `-1`. (If the selected value matches no enabled tab, the first enabled tab gets tabIndex 0 so the list is still reachable.)
- T5 Keyboard on a focused tab: ArrowRight → next enabled tab, ArrowLeft → previous enabled tab, both wrap around; Home → first enabled tab; End → last enabled tab. The new tab receives DOM focus AND becomes selected (selection follows focus → `onValueChange` fires). Disabled tabs are skipped. Keys call `preventDefault`. Other keys do nothing.
- T6 Tab order is computed from DOM order of the tabs (e.g. querying `[role="tab"]` in the tablist element at key time, or registration in render order), not hardcoded.
- Hostile: all tabs disabled (arrows do nothing, no crash, no infinite loop); only one enabled tab (arrow keeps focus on it); controlled `value` the parent never updates (selection stays put after arrow key, but onValueChange was called with the new value); disabled tab in the middle and at the wrap boundary.

Dialog
- D1 Props: `open: boolean`, `onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void`, `title: ReactNode`, `description?: ReactNode`, `children?: ReactNode`. When `open` is false, nothing is rendered. When true, renders via `createPortal` into `document.body`.
- D2 Renders a backdrop element and inside it an element with `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` → the title element's id (title rendered e.g. as `<h2>`), and `aria-describedby` → description element id only when `description` is provided (no dangling aria-describedby otherwise).
- D3 On open, focus moves into the dialog: first tabbable element inside it; if none, the dialog element itself (which has `tabIndex={-1}`).
- D4 Focus trap: Tab from the last tabbable wraps to the first; Shift+Tab from the first wraps to the last; with zero tabbables, Tab keeps focus on the dialog. Tabbable = a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex] not "-1", excluding disabled ones and elements with `hidden`.
- D5 Escape (keydown anywhere while open, focus inside) calls `onOpenChange(false)`. Clicking (mousedown+click on) the backdrop itself calls `onOpenChange(false)`; clicks inside the dialog content do NOT. A click that starts inside the dialog and ends on the backdrop should not close (check that the pointerdown/mousedown target was the backdrop).
- D6 When the dialog closes (open → false, or unmount while open), focus returns to the element that was focused before it opened (if it's still in the document).
- D7 Works controlled only (open is required) — that's the spec. `onOpenChange` is only called; the dialog doesn't close itself.
- Hostile: dialog with no focusable children; description omitted; opening with nothing focused (document.body) — closing must not throw; the previously focused element removed while dialog open; two Escape presses; reopening the dialog a second time restores focus again correctly.

Combobox
- C1 Props: `label: string`, `options: { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }[]` (export the `ComboboxOption` type), `value: string | null`, `onChange: (value: string | null) => void`, `placeholder?: string`. Value is controlled (as spec'd).
- C2 Markup: a `<label>` tied to an `<input role="combobox">` via htmlFor/id; input has `aria-expanded` (true/false), `aria-controls` → listbox id, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-activedescendant` → the active option's id only when the popup is open and an option is active (attribute absent otherwise). Popup: `role="listbox"` element with an id and `aria-labelledby` → label id; options `role="option"` with unique ids, `aria-selected` (true for the currently selected value), `aria-disabled="true"` for disabled ones.
- C3 When the input isn't being edited, its text shows the selected option's label (or empty when `value` is null). If the parent changes `value`, the displayed text updates.
- C4 Typing opens the listbox and filters options whose label contains the typed text, case-insensitively (substring match; trim not required but empty query shows all options). The active option resets when the query changes (to the first enabled match, or none — pick one and document it).
- C5 ArrowDown: if closed, opens the listbox (and activates first enabled option, or the selected one if present); if open, moves to the next enabled option. ArrowUp moves to the previous enabled option (when closed, opens it and activates the last enabled option or the selected one). Disabled options are skipped. Whether movement wraps — pick wrap and document it. Arrow keys `preventDefault`. The active option has some indicator besides aria-activedescendant (e.g. `data-active="true"`) so styling is possible.
- C6 Enter with an active enabled option: calls `onChange(option.value)`, closes the listbox, input text becomes that label. Enter with no active option: does nothing (doesn't throw, doesn't submit-select). Clicking an enabled option selects it the same way (use onMouseDown preventDefault so the input keeps focus, or handle focus properly); clicking a disabled option does nothing and does not close.
- C7 Escape while open: closes the listbox, does NOT call onChange, and restores the input text to the selected option's label (revert the typed query). Escape while closed: optional to clear — just don't crash; document whatever you do.
- C8 When the filter matches nothing, the popup shows a "No results" message (e.g. a `role="status"` or plain element inside/near the listbox with the text "No results"), `aria-activedescendant` is absent, and Enter does nothing.
- C9 Blur (focus leaving the input, not to an option) closes the listbox and reverts the text to the selected label. Clearing the input text entirely and blurring/Enter is allowed to call `onChange(null)` — document it; at minimum `value={null}` displays an empty input.
- C10 Clicking the input or focusing it does not need to open the popup (optional); typing must.
- Hostile: query with regex special chars like `(` or `.*` (must be literal substring, no throw); all options disabled (arrows do nothing, no active descendant); empty `options` array (shows "No results" when opened); option values that contain spaces (ids still valid — use index-based ids); `value` that matches no option (input empty, no crash); two Comboboxes on one page with distinct ids; ArrowDown when the only matching option is disabled.

General
- G1 `src/index.ts` exports `Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Dialog, Combobox` and their props types (`TabsProps`, `TabListProps`, `TabProps`, `TabPanelProps`, `DialogProps`, `ComboboxProps`, `ComboboxOption`).
- G2 Fully typed, no `any` in public types. Components ship no styles; pass through `className` where reasonable.
- G3 Tests in `tests/<Component>.test.tsx` using Testing Library + user-event covering each criterion above, including the hostile inputs.
- G4 README: install/usage snippet, then a section per component with a props table (name, type, default/required, description) and a keyboard table that matches the code exactly, plus `pnpm test` / `pnpm typecheck` instructions.
- G5 `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` both pass.

1. Dialog initial-focus guard regression (src/Dialog.tsx). The current guard `if (!document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]')) (first ?? dialog).focus();` breaks the common sequential case: outer Dialog is open, user clicks a button INSIDE it that sets inner `open` → the inner dialog mounts, but activeElement (the button) is inside the outer dialog, so the inner dialog never takes focus. Fix: add a React context in Dialog.tsx that carries the chain of ancestor dialog elements (each DialogContent provides `[...parentChain, dialogRef]` or similar, read via refs at effect time). In the initial-focus effect, skip taking focus only if `document.activeElement` is inside a `[role="dialog"]` element that is neither this dialog nor one of its React ancestors (that's the simultaneous-mount case where a nested child already focused itself). Otherwise focus (first tabbable ?? dialog). Tests: (a) sequential: outer open with a button "Open inner" that sets inner open → after click, focus is inside the inner dialog (first tabbable); Escape → only inner onOpenChange(false) fires; after inner closes, focus returns to the "Open inner" button. (b) Existing simultaneous-mount nested test still passes (inner keeps focus, Escape closes only inner).

2. Combobox active option on typing (src/Combobox.tsx). Currently `handleInput` always sets active to -1, so typing "app" then Enter does nothing. Change: when the new query's trimmed text is non-empty, active resets to the first enabled match in the filtered list (stepEnabled(filtered, -1, 1)); when the trimmed query is empty, active is -1 (so Enter clears to null as now). Restore tests: type "app" + Enter selects the first enabled match; typing where the first match is disabled activates the next enabled match; cleared text + Enter still calls onChange(null). Update README's description of the active-option reset accordingly.
